problem_description: Investigate the average energetic evolution in eV of a Pt–Pd alloy, and average temperature in K, during temperature cycling and Monte Carlo atom-type swapping using molecular dynamics simulations in LAMMPS. The system should be simulated using `metal` units, non-periodic boundary conditions in all three directions (`boundary f f f`), and the `atomic` atom style. The initial configuration should be read from the `PtPd.data` data file. Pt–Pd interactions should be described using the embedded atom method (EAM) alloy potential through the `eam/alloy` pair style and the `PtPd.set` potential file, with atom type 1 assigned to Pt and atom type 2 assigned to Pd. A timestep of 0.001 ps should be used throughout the simulation. Before the temperature-cycling stages, initial atomic velocities should be generated at 600 K using a Gaussian distribution with random seed 5728459, with rotational degrees of freedom enabled. The system should have reflective walls at the lower and upper edges of the simulation box in the x, y, and z directions using the `wall/reflect` fix. Per-atom potential energy and kinetic energy should be calculated using the `pe/atom` and `ke/atom` computes, respectively. First, the system should undergo a heating stage using an NVT ensemble applied to all atoms, with the target temperature ramped linearly from 300 K to 750 K and a temperature damping parameter of 5.0 ps. This stage should be performed for 10,000 timesteps, corresponding to 10 ps. During this stage, atom ID, atom type, x, y, and z coordinates, per-atom potential energy, and per-atom kinetic energy should be recorded every 10,000 timesteps in `1.lammpstrj`. Next, the system should be equilibrated at a constant temperature of 750 K using an NVT ensemble with a temperature damping parameter of 5.0 ps. This stage should also be performed for 10,000 timesteps, corresponding to 10 ps, with the atom ID, atom type, coordinates, per-atom potential energy, and per-atom kinetic energy recorded every 10,000 timesteps in `2.lammpstrj`. The system should then undergo Pt–Pd atom-type swapping at 750 K using the `atom/swap` fix while the 750 K NVT condition remains active. Atom-type exchange attempts should be performed every 1 timestep, with 5 swap attempts per exchange event, using random seed 654321 and a target temperature of 750 K. Kinetic-energy changes should be excluded from the atom-swap acceptance criterion using `ke no`, and swapping should be restricted to atom types 1 and 2, corresponding to Pt and Pd. This atom-swapping stage should be performed for 10,000 timesteps, corresponding to 10 ps, with atom ID, atom type, coordinates, per-atom potential energy, and per-atom kinetic energy recorded every 10,000 timesteps in `3.lammpstrj`. After the 750 K atom-swapping stage, the system should be cooled from 750 K to 300 K using an NVT ensemble with a temperature damping parameter of 5.0 ps. The cooling stage should be performed for 10,000 timesteps, corresponding to 10 ps, with the resulting trajectory recorded every 10,000 timesteps in `4.lammpstrj`. The same per-atom quantities should be recorded: atom ID, atom type, x, y, z coordinates, per-atom potential energy, and per-atom kinetic energy. Finally, the system should be maintained at a constant temperature of 300 K using an NVT ensemble with a temperature damping parameter of 5.0 ps while simultaneously performing Pt–Pd atom-type swapping. The `atom/swap` fix should attempt exchanges every 1 timestep, with 5 swap attempts per exchange event, using random seed 654321 and a target temperature of 300 K. Kinetic-energy changes should again be excluded from the acceptance criterion using `ke no`, and exchanges should be restricted to atom types 1 and 2. This final NVT and atom-swapping stage should be performed for 10,000 timesteps, corresponding to 10 ps, with the trajectory recorded every 10,000 timesteps in `5.lammpstrj`. Thermodynamic information should be reported every 100 timesteps throughout the simulation using the LAMMPS `thermo 100` setting. The complete simulation sequence consists of five consecutive stages: heating from 300 K to 750 K, equilibration at 750 K, Pt–Pd atom-type swapping at 750 K, cooling from 750 K to 300 K, and simultaneous NVT equilibration and Pt–Pd atom-type swapping at 300 K. Each stage consists of 10,000 timesteps, giving a total of 50,000 timesteps and a total simulation time of 50 ps.
